summary.intent: Evaluate how well the Wisp plugins served front-end work and design ideation across the orin-dx and pages projects, then act on the findings by finishing the v5 plugin set (wisp, packs, mason) and making the docs use-focused, complete and diagram-current.
summary.outcome: Four investigations showed the plugin pipeline was too rigid for exploratory design and had no visual capability. v5 migrations were opened in Pages and Caliper. The docs, READMEs, diagrams, mason plugin and authoring rules were rewritten for v5, `just check` exits 0, and the work was committed on chore/v5-docs-and-mason.

repo: The v5 plugin set is wisp (entry skill `work` with modes explore/spike/fix/build/check/ship), wisp-packs, courier, muse and mason. Review is risk-tiered through a single wisp:verifier, and the old spec/plan/gate pipeline is retired.

Generated files (marketplace.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, dist/codex/**, plugin manifests) are produced by `just claude-manifests-sync` and `just marketplace-sync`. Run both before `just check`, and edit sources under plugins/ and harnesses/codex/, not dist/.
Published schemas in shared/schemas are immutable. Removing fields such as `spec_hash` in plan@1, or dropping the orphaned schemas, is a breaking change, so the 35 old-pipeline schemas stay.
The constitution block embedded in agent files must stay byte-identical across agents. It lives in the agent files, not in shared/constitution.md.

validate-handback.py denies an invalid handback up to 3 times per agent (MAX_DENIALS=3), has RETRY_CAP=1, routes only wisp:verifier, and uses the WISP_HANDBACK_TRACE switch. Docs were checked against it.
The Pages repo's AGENTS.md line 46 says not to open PRs with gh, because Entire opens PRs from the branch trail. Caliper follows the same note.

ARCHITECTURE.md anchors the README depends on are #7-agent-authoring-principles and #11-validation-and-release-model. The old #6-verification-protocol is now #4-verification-protocol, and hooks are at #5-hooks-and-where-they-run.
Codex has no hooks and Antigravity delivery is unverified. Behaviour that must hold on those harnesses has to live in skill text.
`just mermaid` parses all mermaid blocks in the repo (16), and `just check` is the full repo gate.

code.finding: The docstring and a comment still claimed muse registers the handback hook and has an exit gate. In v5 muse has no hooks.json and ROUTES lists only wisp:verifier. Both were corrected.
The pre-v5 Cognitive Modes table with 'do not combine modes' was replaced by a context-or-risk split of agents with wisp:verifier, adversary and recon as the worked examples.

workflow: Mechanical scans over ~/.claude/projects jsonl files, counting Skill and Agent tool_use, were a quick way to measure real plugin usage. Plugin agents appeared in only 2 of ~810 files, most of which were subagent transcripts, not sessions.
Subagent reports contain unverified claims. Spot-checking them against the files (the hook denial cap, the README anchors) before committing caught nothing wrong but was cheap.

Splitting parallel docs agents by file ownership still caused overlap. v5-docs edited README.md before the scope change reached it, and sync tools rewrote files that other agents had bumped, so ownership needs to be stated up front.
Specs written before visuals settle cause gate churn. Rendered options on real pages, picked with short codes, worked much better for design decisions than text descriptions.
The user's own words in the sessions ('lean less on the specs and tests... those come when we narrow it down') were the strongest evidence for the rigidity hypothesis.

friction: The session count was initially wrong. The orin-dx and pages dirs held only a few real sessions, and the rest were subagent transcripts.
Muse's docs pointed to a ranger accessibility taxonomy that does not exist, so implemented accessibility was never checked.
Spec and plan files of 60-130 KB stalled agent streams, and the 17 failed agent tasks were never explained.
The exit-gate loops were churny. SPEC-001 needed 13 verdicts, 10 of them fails. The orchestrator carried on past the gate's escalate after 3 retries without asking the user.
The Pages PR #45 was opened with gh against that repo's own rule, because the brief to the agent was wrong. It is a draft and easy to close.
Cleanup of Entire findings and merged remote branches was denied by the classifier earlier and needs a retry.
v5-docs and v5-readme both edited root README.md, and sync tools regenerated files containing another agent's changes, which made attribution confusing.
The Claude `evaluate` skill cites docs/evaluation-runbook.md, which ships with the repo but not with the installed plugin or the Codex bundle.
open_items: Approve Entire trail #416 and the repo migration PRs. Run `just release` from main to cut 5.0.0, which publishes and stays with the user.
Decide whether to close Pages PR #45 and redo it as an Entire trail.
Callisto and Monokl v5 migrations are still finishing, and their trails need reporting.
Apply the three queued `wisp` tweaks in one small PR: load references by mode, mention packs in `work`'s start step, and reword the Stop-hook line in `finish` for question-only turns.
Cleanup: resolve three Entire findings on trail #386, delete merged remote branches including the stray v5-core, and list stale Callisto and Caliper trails without closing them.
Decide whether to remove mason's own worker agents, scaffolder and schema-designer.
Decide on the orphaned schemas and references (arch-spec@1, implementation-review@1/2, implementation-context@1, the spec_hash field in plan@1, about eight unused shared references).

Build a UI/front-end pack. A brand source of truth is undecided, and the design gaps remain: no sketch or visual-exploration mode, no render-based evidence, no decision log, and no promote-prototype-to-spec path.
Verify Antigravity delivery, including `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` handling and the unverified hooks and pack injection.

After 1-2 weeks of real use, measure gate rounds, turns and tokens with tools/transcript-metrics.py, then decide on pruning the verifier (870 words) and modes.md (794 words). Also revisit adversary's candidate-assessment@1 schema fit and the pack taste calls (expect/panic!, camino, any in TS, a third house pack).
apps/orin-dx/src/data/pages/wisp.ts in Pages still describes the old Smith/Scribe flow in site copy. The old plugins-guide worktree is also still on disk.
Verify the README's unverified facts: the .claude/settings.json extraKnownMarketplaces snippet, and the Antigravity `agy plugin install` command.
